description: WHICH ENDPOINTS A PAYEE SELLS, or which ones match some text. The sharpest check a payment can get is the endpoint being bought, and until this a caller had to know its URL by heart. Nearly every catalogued resource names a payee, and the catalogue holds tens of thousands of them. Every field is the SELLER’s own catalogue entry and never our reading of it, and a listing is not evidence that the endpoint answers — `test_purchase` knocks on it. `priceUsd` is their published price and `priceRaw` is the figure in the asset’s own base units; the two are different claims. FREE.

payee.description: An address, to list what it sells.

q.description: Part of a URL, matched case-insensitively.

name: list_x402_endpoints

capped.description: TRUE where the page came back full, so there are probably more; FALSE means the catalogue holds no further match and the list is everything we have, not just the first slice. This replaced a declared `limit` that the answer never carried — the envelope owns the paging keys — and it answers the question that field was for in one go.

count.description: How many came back, which is at most `limit` and says nothing about how many exist.

items.description: One per catalogued endpoint: `resource`, `payTo`, `priceUsd` and `priceRaw`, `asset`, `network`, the seller’s own `description` and when the listing was last seen — every one of those is the SELLER’s claim. `seenByUs` is the only field here that is OURS and the only one they cannot write: `state` (`answering`, `not-answering`, `unconfirmed` — one failure, which is a reason to ask again and not a finding — `seen-once`, or `never-knocked`), `answered` of `knocks`, `lastKnocked`, and an outage as a RANGE in `downAtLeastHours` / `downAtMostHours` rather than as a duration, because a stop happened somewhere between two knocks and that window is as wide as the gap between them. `never-knocked` and `seen-once` are statements about OUR reach, not about the seller, and today they cover most of the catalogue. The full timeline is on `test_purchase`.

says.description: What the list is and is not: the seller’s own entries, and a listing is not evidence the endpoint answers.

title: What this address sells
